chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding

two men who joined together to cut off a man's hand. He said: 'If he (the victim) wishes to have both their hands cut off, he shall pay them both the blood money of one hand, which they divide between themselves, and then their hands are cut off; and if he wishes, he may take from both of them the blood money of one hand.'
He said: 'And if the hand of only one of the two is cut off, the one whose hand was not cut off must pay a quarter of the blood money to the one whose hand was cut off.'

key_terms.اجتمع على: Joined together in committing — collective liability in criminal participation
key_terms.حد: Hadd — a fixed Quranic punishment for certain crimes
key_terms.دية: Blood money (diya/wergild) — the financial compensation prescribed for bodily harm or death in Islamic law
key_terms.قصاص: Qisas — the principle of retaliatory punishment in kind (cutting for cutting)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when two people together cut off someone's hand?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) addresses the jurisprudential ruling when two persons together commit the crime of cutting off another person's hand (a hadd crime requiring qisas). The Imam explains two options for the victim: he may either have both offenders' hands cut off as qisas (provided he first pays each one half the blood money of a hand, to compensate for the one hand effectively replacing two), or he may forgo qisas and instead take the full blood money for one hand from both offenders. A further sub-ruling establishes that if the victim elects to execute qisas against only one offender, the one spared must compensate the one whose hand was cut off with a quarter of the full blood money, to equalize the burden between the two joint offenders.
